summary: This tutorial covers how to use command line arguments in C programming on Ubuntu 11.10 using GCC compiler version 4.6.1. It explains that `argc` represents the number of command-line arguments passed to the program, while `argv` holds the actual arguments as strings. The first element of `argv` (index 0) contains the program name, and subsequent elements contain the actual arguments passed to the program. The tutorial demonstrates this by compiling and running a sample C program that prints out the command-line arguments. When the user inputs "sunday monday tuesday", the program outputs "Arguments: 4" because there are four arguments including the program name. The tutorial concludes by emphasizing the importance of understanding command-line arguments for passing parameters to programs and provides a link to the full video for further learning.
